Whomever you endorse will have a sacred responsibility to promote and defend our party, its principles and its people against all of the inevitable attacks from the liberal media and the “progressive” special interests. If I earn your endorsement on May 14, you can rely on my past record of supporting our party, our principles and our people – even against the withering assaults from the Left. Case in point: I actively supported President Trump in 2020. [](http://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=3fcb452ec5b84111b419c69f3fa50201&_m=6480ea46a8e94f60b2862d3758a6c6d1&_e=J2lShMXAvuIpJkSsvFnWx2tAm66rZdr206ITQ6yoA0i8J8URRAPfNR5NhkNMAY89SzloAvEgQ8nvDGg4Gn2TUsWS6IoBY_giIE36kQI5dOoRIIYVzPNBN2CdwiplY3yaW8u5tDdz5_BXAZJIcuuG8F9DGhyJAn8kgix4N0341Bl1LF4qGe9Q1CEEa8S2sBFA4wi_8FO5_LH_aA8Bz1DysMycRd86f7JNY5U9U7lLNstMqbDGn28sMI9Qs8LuzSQ_qw3yD29clT_vKeJ1-WRhOTvVjqgIeHiXNzVmISAO-0hjzcmdX2Skob_RiqVFiXQ7sCjAPVKNMzF1FCaExFXaIEWsbCmp1sbHWaBAKm-1DX4%3D) [**Stand Up for Minnesota! >> Donate NOW**](http://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=3fcb452ec5b84111b419c69f3fa50201&_m=6480ea46a8e94f60b2862d3758a6c6d1&_e=J2lShMXAvuIpJkSsvFnWx2tAm66rZdr206ITQ6yoA0i8J8URRAPfNR5NhkNMAY89SzloAvEgQ8nvDGg4Gn2TUsWS6IoBY_giIE36kQI5dOoRIIYVzPNBN2CdwiplY3yaW8u5tDdz5_BXAZJIcuuG8BkaqETb-OlAEBYCybCJZSe3Mb7xlOCCYt2goNYGPzT27Xn4M5i2Iwb5iWs1v65-R1OAv0U9ICjV_n7x6op0CSIw0CUajSPDlyNlpeLn9HogIgMemII7D0teZKLM7zzXz-8-E8LQiuhGqC56Tzwbvxserzao5idGyyeccexbtVQsnEknD00CU1C4zrPvRgKkUw7wM92JS3D7xzIYhquizwU%3D) My reasons were simple: President Trump deserved re-election. He did much good for our country. He was the better man and better candidate. He gave voice to the aspirations of many of us who have seen our country and its working- and middle-classes ignored and abused. And, most importantly from the standpoint of party loyalty, he was an incumbent Republican president seeking re-election and relying on our help. As then-Senate Majority Leader, I knew that my fellow Republican senators needed a strong showing of party unity to help them turn out their base voters in their districts in order to win against enormous odds. Remember that our Senate GOP majority was then (and remains for the time being) the only bulwark of freedom at the state Capitol against the united forces of Governor Walz and the House DFL majority. If we failed to maintain our majority, Minnesota would suddenly veer hard Left. I defended President Trump vigorously on the campaign trail in 2020. It was the right thing to do politically for the cause of re-electing my caucus’s majority. And it was the right thing to do morally. I wrote op-ed pieces urging the President’s re-election, published in newspapers across the state. I did many media appearances advocating for President Trump. I proudly and unequivocally defended his record and advocated for him. I did what a party leader should do. I worked hard for the GOP ticket and defended our people – in this case, President Trump and my caucus colleagues, plus House candidates and others – irrespective of any minor disagreements that any of us may have with each other. And that’s what I will do as your endorsee for governor: Advocate for our ticket – without fear or temporizing when the onslaught of attacks come from Walz, the DFL party, and their host of allies. Can the other candidates running for governor say the same? I don’t remember Neil Shah campaigning vigorously for President Trump in 2020 anywhere. Of course, just two years before that, Shah had contributed money to Tim Walz and other Democrats, so it wouldn’t be shocking if he had sat out the Trump re-election effort. Kendall Qualls, to his credit, running in 2020 for Congress in the Third District, didn’t repudiate the President. He didn’t exactly give Donald Trump his vigorous, full-throated endorsement – “His style’s not my style” Qualls said – but he said he supported the President. And what did Scott Jenson do for President Trump’s re-election effort? Well, you no doubt have heard about, and perhaps even seen, the YouTube [video](http://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=3fcb452ec5b84111b419c69f3fa50201&_m=6480ea46a8e94f60b2862d3758a6c6d1&_e=J2lShMXAvuIpJkSsvFnWxxVoMNuWRlXWkjpkUFHFciGw5X44OKkXb-ob7xscfwpHaNI2ubna3dryfDBrmnaQs993Igbf4VDvJb506UyVtMIaEQf9thchz_9NR2ju0FVQyeT3w19wZwOEGaNA9AdvnrczQDk7pF7xqZaM60kEFqILfRZqifqUtNylZq2NQWZHEdSCdDQdPFBqyRpxJc-5_CRHf2vlPQXPa_4-8APGkDl6lXTNPcnO9LwRaUbjSy0uBzaRaJScxwY1Rbl9VFjEoKVkscCnZRC0btnXSeIAvuo%3D) of Jensen speaking at a campaign rally for Libertarian presidential candidate Jo Jorgenson on October 30, 2020, in Victoria, Minnesota. As President Trump was fighting for his re-election, ostensibly “Republican” state Senator Scott Jensen was showing support for a Trump rival. He didn’t need to do that. Jensen was retiring from a safe Republican seat. Minnesota was still theoretically a battleground state. Other Republicans needed Trump’s ability to turn out the conservative base to ensure their re-elections in a tough year for Republicans. If Scott Jensen didn’t support President Trump, he could have simply been...silent. Instead, Scott Jensen betrayed an incumbent Republican president fighting a pitched battle for his re-election in a swing state – and he betrayed the rest of us who were working hard for the success of the entire ticket in an extraordinarily tough political environment. And this guy thinks he should be the leader of our ticket this November? We have a historic – no exaggeration – opportunity to win the governorship and both houses of the Minnesota Legislature in November, along with other statewide offices and more congressional seats. Even the liberal national media is starting to talk about the possibility of 2022 being a Republican “wave election.” This year we have the greatest chance of winning a sweeping Republican victory in Minnesota for the first time since 1966. I’ve proven myself to be a team player and a team leader. I led the Senate GOP’s successful opposition to a myriad of insane policies pushed by the House DFL and Governor. I defended my colleagues when they faced attack after attack, and successfully led our caucus’s first-ever back-to-back legislative majorities, raising a record amount of money for the Senate GOP campaign committee. In the process, I also advocated for other Republican candidates for other office. I did my job as party leader in the Senate and I delivered. Ridiculous critics can smear me and my legislative colleagues as “RINOs.” I trust that you can see through their lies. Some of them claim I didn’t do enough to rein in Walz when, in truth, I was the one who employed what powers I had as Senate Majority Leader to force Walz to finally abandon his regime of ruling by executive orders. These critics were not in the arena. They were not defending President on the campaign trail in 2020. No, they were keyboard warriors at best – while the rest of us were fighting hand-to-hand combat with the Left every single day to protect our values, principles, culture, and freedoms. My candidacy isn’t about me. It’s about achieving success for the entire team. I’ve already proven that I can run a statewide campaign effort; help elect and re-elect fellow Republicans against the forces stacked against us; raise the money needed to compete and win; handle the hostile media; and face off against Tim Walz and beat him on the battlefield of ideas. clean_body: Dear Republican friend, Our party’s endorsee for governor will lead the top of our ticket in our battle to restore freedom against the Left DFL. Whomever you endorse will have a sacred responsibility to promote and defend our party, its principles and its people against all of the inevitable attacks from the liberal media and the “progressive” special interests. If I earn your endorsement on May 14, you can rely on my past record of supporting our party, our principles and our people – even against the withering assaults from the Left. Case in point: I actively supported President Trump in 2020. My reasons were simple: President Trump deserved re-election. He did much good for our country. He was the better man and better candidate. He gave voice to the aspirations of many of us who have seen our country and its working- and middle-classes ignored and abused. And, most importantly from the standpoint of party loyalty, he was an incumbent Republican president seeking re-election and relying on our help. As then-Senate Majority Leader, I knew that my fellow Republican senators needed a strong showing of party unity to help them turn out their base voters in their districts in order to win against enormous odds. Remember that our Senate GOP majority was then (and remains for the time being) the only bulwark of freedom at the state Capitol against the united forces of Governor Walz and the House DFL majority. If we failed to maintain our majority, Minnesota would suddenly veer hard Left. I defended President Trump vigorously on the campaign trail in 2020. It was the right thing to do politically for the cause of re-electing my caucus’s majority. And it was the right thing to do morally. I wrote op-ed pieces urging the President’s re-election, published in newspapers across the state. I did many media appearances advocating for President Trump. I proudly and unequivocally defended his record and advocated for him. I did what a party leader should do. I worked hard for the GOP ticket and defended our people – in this case, President Trump and my caucus colleagues, plus House candidates and others – irrespective of any minor disagreements that any of us may have with each other. And that’s what I will do as your endorsee for governor: Advocate for our ticket – without fear or temporizing when the onslaught of attacks come from Walz, the DFL party, and their host of allies. Can the other candidates running for governor say the same? I don’t remember Neil Shah campaigning vigorously for President Trump in 2020 anywhere. Of course, just two years before that, Shah had contributed money to Tim Walz and other Democrats, so it wouldn’t be shocking if he had sat out the Trump re-election effort. Kendall Qualls, to his credit, running in 2020 for Congress in the Third District, didn’t repudiate the President. He didn’t exactly give Donald Trump his vigorous, full-throated endorsement – “His style’s not my style” Qualls said – but he said he supported the President. And what did Scott Jenson do for President Trump’s re-election effort? Well, you no doubt have heard about, and perhaps even seen, the YouTube of Jensen speaking at a campaign rally for Libertarian presidential candidate Jo Jorgenson on October 30, 2020, in Victoria, Minnesota. As President Trump was fighting for his re-election, ostensibly “Republican” state Senator Scott Jensen was showing support for a Trump rival. He didn’t need to do that. Jensen was retiring from a safe Republican seat. Minnesota was still theoretically a battleground state. Other Republicans needed Trump’s ability to turn out the conservative base to ensure their re-elections in a tough year for Republicans. If Scott Jensen didn’t support President Trump, he could have simply been...silent. Instead, Scott Jensen betrayed an incumbent Republican president fighting a pitched battle for his re-election in a swing state – and he betrayed the rest of us who were working hard for the success of the entire ticket in an extraordinarily tough political environment. And this guy thinks he should be the leader of our ticket this November? We have a historic – no exaggeration – opportunity to win the governorship and both houses of the Minnesota Legislature in November, along with other statewide offices and more congressional seats. Even the liberal national media is starting to talk about the possibility of 2022 being a Republican “wave election.” This year we have the greatest chance of winning a sweeping Republican victory in Minnesota for the first time since 1966. I’ve proven myself to be a team player and a team leader. I led the Senate GOP’s successful opposition to a myriad of insane policies pushed by the House DFL and Governor. I defended my colleagues when they faced attack after attack, and successfully led our caucus’s first-ever back-to-back legislative majorities, raising a record amount of money for the Senate GOP campaign committee. In the process, I also advocated for other Republican candidates for other office. I did my job as party leader in the Senate and I delivered. Ridiculous critics can smear me and my legislative colleagues as “RINOs.” I trust that you can see through their lies. Some of them claim I didn’t do enough to rein in Walz when, in truth, I was the one who employed what powers I had as Senate Majority Leader to force Walz to finally abandon his regime of ruling by executive orders. These critics were not in the arena. They were not defending President on the campaign trail in 2020. No, they were keyboard warriors at best – while the rest of us were fighting hand-to-hand combat with the Left every single day to protect our values, principles, culture, and freedoms. My candidacy isn’t about me. It’s about achieving success for the entire team. I’ve already proven that I can run a statewide campaign effort; help elect and re-elect fellow Republicans against the forces stacked against us; raise the money needed to compete and win; handle the hostile media; and face off against Tim Walz and beat him on the battlefield of ideas. I did it as Senate Majority Leader and I will do it as your endorsee for governor if you bestow that humbling honor on me. Thank you, Senator Paul Gazelka Candidate for Governor | | | | ---|---|--- Paid for and Provided by Gazelka for Governor P.O. Box 175 Little Falls, MN 56345

But we’re not taking anything for granted in this race.

DeSantis and his right-wing, billionaire backers won’t go quietly, so Charlie is committed to building the largest grassroots movement in Florida history to defeat this failed governor. | | |

| | | April 29, 2022 Hi Friends, The fight for free speech intensified this week all across our country. From Southwest Washington to Washington, DC, the headlines were startling. Let’s start with the national situation first. We all watched with a mixture of curiosity and hope as Elon Musk purchased Twitter. Musk claims he wants a level playing field without the censorship of information or opinion. This is offensive to the Democrats, of course, and predictably, the far left response came quickly. Celebrities and politicians cried foul as they realized their iron-fisted grasp of this popular communication platform might be lost or weakened. It’s not enough that they control mainstream media, schools, colleges, universities, woke corporations and the pathetic entertainment industry. They are terrified that the truth might leak out about things like Russian collusion, Hunter’s laptop, election integrity, medical freedom and so much more. It was alarming to learn that before Elon Musk had even written the check, Joe Biden and his handlers were putting a diabolical backup plan in motion. On Wednesday, a new federal "Disinformation Governance Board" was announced to combat "disinformation in the 2022 midterms.” Eerily similar to the “Ministry of Truth” described by George Orwell in his classic novel 1984, this new censorship team will operate under the authority of the Department of Homeland Security. Talk about irony. Nothing could make our nation less secure (or less American) than censorship. Freedom-loving, hard-working Americans are learning a very hard lesson right now. Leadership matters. Under the Democrats, inflation is skyrocketing. Our borders are not secure. Our education system is broken and our Constitution is being trampled. We need new leadership. From our school boards to the White House, we are facing a crisis in leadership. I’m running to change that. I’m running to bring common-sense solutions and real, engaged representation to DC on the behalf of this place that I love and have served for nearly twenty years. To do that, I need your prayers and your financial support. You can support my run here:****
**[_donate today_](https://heidistjohnforcongress.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=46e715d1574a19c15defda548&id=6632fbe80d&e=b0bcc6b4f9)**

For Freedom,

_Candidate for Congress, SW Washington_
Standing Up For What We Believe
---
| | **News and Media**
---
| Here in Southwest Washington, Portland carpetbagger Joe Kent continues to engage in a variety of intimidation and bullying tactics aimed at my campaign. He is denying recent stories in local and national papers about his own campaign leadership, hoping to keep his [dirty campaign tactics](https://heidistjohnforcongress.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=46e715d1574a19c15defda548&id=b96c9a44af&e=b0bcc6b4f9), his political past, and his [socialist policy ideas](https://heidistjohnforcongress.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=46e715d1574a19c15defda548&id=ddca455ad5&e=b0bcc6b4f9) from leaking out to District voters. I urge you to watch our local campaigns closely. People will govern how they campaign. We cannot afford to let our district fall into the hands of an unknown Portland Democrat who is masquerading as a Conservative. Re-electing our current congresswoman assures that SW Washington will continue to be represented by a fiscal Democrat. Jaime is no longer representing our Republican values, and her [voting record](https://heidistjohnforcongress.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=46e715d1574a19c15defda548&id=81fd247401&e=b0bcc6b4f9) shows it.

subject: They want to throw Marjorie off the ballot

body:
[](http://asg.vervemail9.com/ct/60264024:JBcnZdoN5:m:1:3103520637:2F354746B0931258197007F7C6E38FA8:r "Headline") Dear Peter, Deflect. Distract. Defame. These are the tactics of desperate candidates. And while there are a lot of "Ds" in those words, these aren't the actions of a Democrat, but a Republican. Bad Brad Raffensperger turned a blind eye to the fraud in Georgia's 2020 elections. Now, any candidate who questions how Brad conducts elections has a target on their back. **[He is again proving he is unfit to serve and that's why I'm seeking your immediate contribution of $25, $50, $100, or any amount you can afford to ensure I end his political career in November.](http://asg.vervemail9.com/ct/60264024:JBcnZdoN5:m:1:3103520637:2F354746B0931258197007F7C6E38FA8:r "He is again proving he is unfit to serve and
that’s why I’m seeking your immediate contribution of $25, $50, $100, or any amount you can afford to ensure I end his political career in
November.")** My friend and fellow Georgian, Marjorie Taylor Greene, has been a champion for America, freedom, and fairness, but Brad Raffensperger and his ilk don't like that one bit. A lawsuit has been filed against Marjorie to keep her off the ballot in November. Why? Because her political opponents are creating the false narrative that Marjorie is an extremist. In reality, Marjorie has been a champion for due process, fairness, and accountability. Now Brad Raffensperger is asking an administrative law judge to determine whether Rep. Greene is qualified for office, and in that hearing "the entire burden is placed [upon the candidate] to affirmatively establish [their] eligibility for office," according to the suit. **_Translation: Guilty until proven innocent._** **[We need to end political witch hunts and that's why I need your IMMEDIATE donation to help keep Bad Brad from winning in May!](http://asg.vervemail9.com/ct/60264024:JBcnZdoN5:m:1:3103520637:2F354746B0931258197007F7C6E38FA8:r "We
need to end political witch hunts and that’s why I need your IMMEDIATE donation to help keep Bad Brad from winning in May!")** [](http://asg.vervemail9.com/ct/60264024:JBcnZdoN5:m:1:3103520637:2F354746B0931258197007F7C6E38FA8:r "Trump")Attempts to keep Marjorie off the ballot are tantamount to a modern-day witch hunt. The left used this playbook in their efforts to impeach Donald Trump and I won't sit on the sidelines and allow their despicable tactics to succeed. **[Will you dig deep with a donation of $500, $250, $100, or any amount you can afford to help me win my race to be Georgia's next Secretary of State?](http://asg.vervemail9.com/ct/60264024:JBcnZdoN5:m:1:3103520637:2F354746B0931258197007F7C6E38FA8:r "Will you dig deep with a donation of $500,
$250, $100, or any amount you can afford to help me win my race to be Georgia’s next Secretary of State?")** Unlike Bad Brad, I'll be an advocate for the voters, ensuring free and fair elections, not changing my tune to fit political narratives or making attempts to throw elected officials off the ballot by violating their civil rights. Bad Brad is a danger to the voters, and we need to defeat him before he can tip the outcome of future elections. He's not a kingmaker and that's why I need your help to remind him that we live in a country where the people will determine their elected representatives, not RINOs to leftists in Washington. **[Please donate today.](http://asg.vervemail9.com/ct/60264024:JBcnZdoN5:m:1:3103520637:2F354746B0931258197007F7C6E38FA8:r "Please donate today.")** In Freedom, Jody Hice

Community is supporting the growth of the 10th District's dynamic economy and many small businesses and local organizations, which are the foundation of our society. Right now, working Americans suffer from the highest inflation rate in decades.

body:
We must sue their radical administrators.
[View this message in your browser](http://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zk8o604ar0mr59eqebcsggrddcleldjefbi8d4ho_rp2ash2s8gb2sbgebjqf99jk5p7atdge5p78d5jmeqjetjjkorrbdt469r31d5jekrq9onicbrb2t9i63gr6chk6cr3as3hc1grccbjcgoefcrgc8pm7cbgc9onbd356ji38o5n6v970sj46oob4pjiegonco70mhij1o5l65iecpj666qb6phgeph6cdj0mdhmfc5lclp238h1e8he4933cli6cp32c3h66oh5u)
We must sue their radical administrators.
| | Dear Fellow Patriot,

This was state-sponsored **censorship** at its finest.

As a public university, SUNY Binghamton administrators have a duty to protect and defend the First Amendment rights of EVERY student to think and speak freely.

Instead, leftist administrators at SUNY Binghamton used your tax dollars to shut down free speech by allowing radical leftist activists to bully, harass, and intimidate conservative students and speakers on campus.

As someone who's been verbally assaulted and abused for my conservative beliefs my entire life, I WILL NOT stand for it.

And now **I'm urgently asking for your help to protect the First Amendment and hold liberal administrators like the ones at SUNY Binghamton accountable for their unconstitutional actions.**

[**Will you help me?**](http://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zq79c4hltun735lukn009blkucom737d6u47mnbo_rp22sh2s8i66pb4cpi64o72cdh2bs)

[](http://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zt39trj00to09jhongr6f01mi8muctgj7ac6jumo_rp22sh2s8i66pb4cpi64o72cdh2bs)

It all started two years ago when a mob of more than 200 leftist activists at SUNY Binghamton University SHUT DOWN a conservative campus lecture.

_The students attempted to host a Young America's Foundation lecture featuring Dr.**Arthur Laffer** , Ronald Reagan's economic policy advisor, on free markets and conservatism, so that their peers could hear your conservative ideas._

But, leftist school administrators at SUNY Binghamton didn't like that one bit.

On the day of the lecture, SUNY Binghamton administrators put the leftist protesters up in the room right next to the lecture hall—specifically so that they could easily barge in and disrupt Dr. **Laffer** 's speech.

Then, the faculty ordered the police to stand down if they got wind of physical violence or threats from the hands of the radical leftist agitators.

When the day came, Dr. **Laffer** walked into the room with hundreds of students patiently waiting to hear what he had to say...

**Before he could even make it up to the podium, the leftist activists swarmed the lecture hall.**

[](http://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zi7rm2eagkmc45p39ebihnv2ru3oasqk59cceec8_rp22sh2s8i66pb4cpi64o72cdh2bs)

With their fists in the air and bullhorns on blast, they belligerently screamed and shouted—drowning out Dr. Laffer with left-wing propaganda.

_**Eventually, a few campus police officers showed up to de-escalate the situation. But rather than remove the leftist activists, the campus police escorted Dr. Laffer out of the auditorium and ended the event!**_

Worse yet, the SUNY Binghamton faculty then decided to SUSPEND the conservative students who organized the event—instead of punishing radical leftists who disrupted Dr. Laffer.

It's bad enough that the students were harassed and intimidated by vile and obnoxious leftist bullies.

But the fact that SUNY Binghamton administrators ENABLED THE LEFTISTS in bullying conservative students makes this a clear violation of the student's rights.

They silenced conservatives. They empowered leftist agitators. And they broke a litany of their own safety rules and protocols regarding incidents like this one.

The good news is that my friends at **Young America's Foundation** are now suing the SUNY Binghamton administrators for unlawfully denying Young America's Foundation, Dr. Laffer and the SUNY conservative students their First Amendment rights.

**But the only way they have a chance of winning the fight for the First Amendment not only at SUNY Binghamton but on campuses across the country is if they gather all the resources necessary to support YAF's EXPERT team of constitutional lawyers and conservative thought leaders.**

[**That's why I'm asking you to help Young America's Foundation protect free speech by sending them a tax-deductible gift of $35 or more today.**](http://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zr8l0fc24nbr8t5c1n4svva551talojt8nemt8oo_rp22sh2s8i66pb4cpi64o72cdh2bs)

You may have heard of Young America's Foundation (YAF) before.

As the largest and most effective conservative youth outreach organization in the country – they have a phenomenal track record of defending free speech in schools and on college campuses.

I know from experience.

A few years ago, YAF was organizing a college lecture tour with me, and one of the stops on the tour was UC Berkeley.

**It was clear that Berkeley administrators didn't want me there.**

They denied me and YAF access to a lecture hall to host my speech, despite the fact they had granted access to numerous leftist speakers in the past.

Apparently, they believed that my conservative message was "too dangerous" and "controversial."

Thankfully, YAF stepped up and sued UC Berkeley for blatantly denying my First Amendment right to free speech and denying the rights of every student who planned on attending.

And with the financial support of conservative folks across the country, YAF is winning the fight for free speech and conservative ideas.

You see, Young America's Foundation doesn't take a single dime from the federal government.

Everything they do to defend free speech and conservative values on hundreds of liberal college campuses across America is thanks to the generous financial support of folks like you.

And now that they're standing up to defend the First Amendment across the country, they need your help.

[**Will you please send a tax-deductible donation of $35, $50, $75 or more to my friends at Young America's Foundation and help them defend our First Amendment rights?**](http://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zn9pjc5e3r44jip6kpk7ts2cqbn074uu3637kujo_rp22sh2s8i66pb4cpi64o72cdh2bs)

**I am so confident in Young America's Foundation that I've chosen them as my exclusive partner for all of my campus lectures and appearances.** In fact, through YAF I've spoken at 60 colleges and universities!

And it's not just me. YAF hosts the most inspiring conservative leaders to introduce your ideas to students in schools. YAF's campus lectures feature NFL star and Congressman **Burgess Owens** , **Newt Gingrich** , **Stephen Crowder** , and **Dinesh D'Souza** , **Katie Pavlich** , and many others. These conservative leaders travel across the country to spread your conservative values and beliefs with hundreds of thousands students (and millions more who watch online).

That's why YAF's lawsuit against the radical administrators of SUNY Binghamton is so important.

One of the most important things they do is prevent leftist college administrators like the ones at SUNY Binghamton from censoring and silencing conservative ideas.

And with your urgent help today, they'll win lawsuits like the one against the radical left bureaucrats at SUNY Binghamton and defend every conservative student's right to think and speak freely.

[**Can I count on you to contribute $25 or more to YAF today and protect the First Amendment?**](http://e.trumptrainnews.com/rd/9z2zp7544rt49jvhugm0etrbhh81ttgkm9o06ae9r00_rp22sh2s8i66pb4cpi64o72cdh2bs)

Sincerely,

_**" I make a hard distinction between Black conservatives and these tokens [Herschel Walker and Senator Tim Scott], who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers."**
--Eli Mystal, MSNBC_

Peter,

I recently wrote to you about a racist article attacking me in _The Nation_.

The author had some pretty heinous things to say because I'm a Black conservative. You may recall this line:

_" Herschel Walker's candidacy is a white insult to Black people."_
Well, Peter, he's back at it again. MSNBC featured this man on their network this week so he could spew even more anti-Black, anti-conservative vitriol in the name of mediocre TV ratings.

He doubled down in his attacks on me. This time he attacked Republican Senator Tim Scott (SC) too. Here's part of what he said:

_" I make a hard distinction between Black conservatives and these tokens [referring to me and Senator Tim Scott], who are out here right now, shucking and jiving for their white handlers." _
**That's racist, disgusting, and sad.**

I never wanted the color of my skin to be a focal point of this Senate campaign, but these attacks on my character and my skin color have gone too far.

**You can help me prove them wrong by standing with me at this critical moment.**

We'd like to show them a groundswell of grassroots support from across Georgia and around the country. **[Can I count on you to help me today?](https://email.vervemail.com/ct/60271492:6mHsqdoTN:m:1:3317145305:921AD758369FCBAEB3C2F1BB5AE1F5E5:r)**

_Just imagine if these comments were made by a conservative about a Black Democrat. They'd be fired immediately after going off air._

**I won't be quiet about this.** This columnist is saying horrible things about fellow human beings based on the color of their skin. That's simply wrong.

**[We hope you'll take a moment today to support our Senate campaign and show the people who want us to fail just how much support there is for Black conservatives in this country.](https://email.vervemail.com/ct/60271492:6mHsqdoTN:m:1:3317145305:921AD758369FCBAEB3C2F1BB5AE1F5E5:r)**

Thanks,

attacking Project Veritas for years. We need to know the details of
any Biden administration discussions targeting the journalists at
Project Veritas.

[INSIDE JW]

BIDEN’S 'MINISTRY OF TRUTH' & ELON MUSK, BIDEN ADMIN TARGETS
O’KEEFE/PROJECT VERITAS, BIOLAB CONCERNS

[Weekly Update]
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=58763&L=27248&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvdmlkZW9zL2JpZGVucy1taW5pc3RyeS1vZi10cnV0aC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=]

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES DOJ, AND HHS FOR COMMUNICATIONS ABOUT PROJECT
VERITAS

From midnight raids to legal maneuvering, the government has been
attacking Project Veritas for years. We need to know the details of
any Biden administration discussions targeting the journalists at
Project Veritas.

We filed three FOIA lawsuits against Departments of Justice (DOJ) and
Health and Human Services (HHS) for communications about Project
Veritas with Pfizer, the _New York Times_ and other outside groups
(_Judicial Watch v Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=58763&L=27247&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLXByb2plY3QtdmVyaXRhcy1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDEwMzUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz]
(No. 1:22-cv-01035)) (_Judicial Watch v Department of Health and Human
Services_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=58763&L=27246&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtaGhzLXByb2plY3QtdmVyaXRhcy1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDEwMzMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz]
(No. 1:22-cv-01033)) (_Judicial Watch v Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=58763&L=27233&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLXByb2plY3QtdmVyaXRhcy1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDEwMzQvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz]
(No. 1:22-cv-01034)).

The lawsuit (No. 1:22-cv-01035) about the FBI’s communications with
Pfizer about Project Veritas was filed after the DOJ failed to respond
to a December 21, 2021, FOIA request for:

* All records of communications between officials in the FBI,
including officials in the offices of the FBI New York Field Office on
the one hand, and employees and representatives of Pfizer Inc. on the
other hand, regarding Project Veritas founder James O’Keefe and/or
Project Veritas.

The lawsuit (No. 1:22-cv-01033) regarding Phoenix Indian Medical
Center communications about Project Veritas was filed after HHS failed
to respond to an October 18, 2021, FOIA request for:

* All records of communications between PIMC officials and/or
employees regarding, concerning, Jodi O’Malley, James O’Keefe
and/or Project Veritas.

The lawsuit (No. 1:22-cv-01034) about the FBI’s communications with
the _New York Times_ about Project Veritas was filed after the DOJ
failed to respond to a November 10, 2021, FOIA request for:

* All records of communications between officials in the FBI,
including officials in the offices of the FBI Director, FBI Deputy
Director, Office of General Counsel, Office of Public Affairs, and/or
the FBI New York Field Office on the one hand, and employees,
contractors, and representatives of The New York Times on the other
hand, regarding the FBI search warrants and raid on the residence of
Project Veritas journalist Spencer Meads on November 4, 2021.
* All records of communications between officials in the FBI,

JUDICIAL WATCH DEMANDS ANSWERS IN COLD CASE MURDER OF NYPD OFFICER

Should we give up on justice even a half century after a murder was
committed? No, we shouldn’t – and especially when it appears there
is an official coverup still underway. Micah Morrison, our chief
investigative reporter, reports the details
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=58763&L=27255&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvanctZGVtYW5kcy1hbnN3ZXJzLWluLWNvbGQtY2FzZS9daW4/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=
our
_Investigative Bulletin_.

> Fifty years ago this month, NYPD Patrolman Phillip Cardillo was
> gunned down inside Louis Farrakhan’s Nation of Islam Mosque in
> Harlem. No one ever did a day in jail for the crime. Is justice in
> the Cardillo case still possible?
>
> The episode quickly became known as “the Harlem Mosque Incident”
> and was immediately engulfed in controversy, with rank-and-file cops
> ordered off the crime scene, a riot in Harlem, racial tensions, and
> a NYPD coverup. An alleged shooter was brought to trial in 1976, but
> a Judicial Watch investigation decades later revealed that key
> evidence was buried, never making it to investigators and
> prosecutors. The defendant was acquitted at a second trial, after
> the first trial resulted in a hung jury. At that point, a special
> prosecutor stepped in. He concluded in a 1980 report that there was
> “a concerted and orchestrated effort by members and former members
> of the Police Department to impede the investigation into the murder
> of Patrolman Philip Cardillo.”
>
> That is, there was a coverup. By the NYPD. Of the murder of one of
> its own.
>
> The case seemed to die. But one cop would not let it go. NYPD
> Detective Randy Jurgensen was the key investigator in the Cardillo
> affair. A legendary figure in New York law-enforcement, Jurgensen
> pursued the case through the two trials to a bitter end. In 2006, he
> published “Circle of Six,” a hard-hitting expose that accused
> New York’s political and police establishment of a “purposeful
> negligence of duty.” Soon after, then-NYPD Police Commissioner Ray
> Kelly ordered the NYPD’s Major Case Squad to take another look at
> the case.
>
> Judicial Watch got involved in the new Cardillo investigation. We
> uncovered critical documents in the case—some never before seen,
> some lost for decades—including a White House tape of President
> Richard Nixon and FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover launching a secret
> program to hunt down cop killers; a secret NYPD report on the
> killing, known as “the Blue Book,” that was withheld from the
> department’s own investigators and Manhattan trial prosecutors;
> the long-lost special prosecutor’s report that raised questions
> about NYPD obstruction of justice; and FBI documents revealing a
> network of (unnamed) informants in the case and hinting at possible
> dirty tricks that may have drawn police to the Harlem mosque that
> fateful day in April. Read Judicial Watch’s investigative report
> here.
>
> Seeking to learn more about the FBI’s role at the Harlem mosque,
> Judicial Watch filed a Freedom of Information Act request for “all
> records concerning the Nation of Islam Mosque #7 in Harlem...
> [including but not limited to] all informant, wiretap, electronic
> surveillance, and physical surveillance records.” The FBI denied
> it had any records related to the mosque. Judicial Watch was not
> satisfied with the FBI response and we filed a FOIA lawsuit seeking
> a more thorough search of records. But no new records were obtained
> from the FBI in the case.
>
> The NYPD took an even more brazen approach when we sought case
> documents under New York’s Freedom of Information Law. The NYPD
> turned us down, claiming it did not have to provide the records
> because the Cardillo case was still “active and ongoing.”
>
> Freedom of information laws have a standard exemption from
> disclosure of material that could impact an ongoing investigation.
> But at the time we filed the FOIL request, the Cardillo case was
> forty-eight years old. There was zero evidence that the case was
> active and ongoing. The NYPD’s refusal to provide any information
> appeared to be an extension of a decades-old coverup.
>
> The coverup was first experienced by early investigators on the
> case, including Jurgensen, and first officially noted in the 1980
> special prosecutor’s report. Judicial Watch decided not to take
> “no” for an answer. We sued the NYPD for documents related to
> the Cardillo investigation.
>
> The case went all the way up to New York’s high court. But in the
> end, we lost. The commanding officer of the NYPD Major Case Squad
> supervising the case claimed under oath that the Cardillo murder
> “is an open investigation and remains actively pursued by the
> NYPD.”
>
> The court noted that the NYPD also “submitted...information
> obtained from the detective leading an active, ongoing investigation
> into the homicide, which included receiving tips from informants and
> conducting interviews of potential witnesses.”
>
> The court ruled that the NYPD “properly withheld the requested
> materials” based on NYPD statements that disclosure would
> interfere with an ongoing investigation. Read the full court
> decision here
>
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=58763&L=27206&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcva2lsbGluZy1jYXJkaWxsby13aGF0LWRpZC10aGUtZmJpLWtub3ctYW5kLXdoZW4tZGlkLXRoZXkta25vdy1pdC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=].
>
> If the NYPD is to be believed, an active pursuit of Cardillo’s
> killer was underway. But it’s been more than two years since the
> New York court, accepting NYPD assurances, rejected Judicial
> Watch’s FOIL request. Is that “active investigation” into the
> Cardillo killing still “ongoing?” What has been accomplished?
>
> Fifty years on, is justice for Phil Cardillo still possible?
> “Remember Cardillo” remains a rallying cry for generations of
> New York City cops—a searing reminder of the dangers of the job,
> of racial strife, and what happens when the brass throws a beat cop
> under the bus.
>
> Critical questions in the case remain unresolved. Who killed
> Cardillo? Who called in the fake “officer in distress” phone
> call that lured Cardillo to the Harlem mosque? Who ordered the
> ubiquitous Nation of Islam guards off the front doors of the mosque
> that morning, allowing Cardillo and other officers to rush in to
> what appears to have been an ambush? What was the role, if any, of
> the FBI in the case? What about the significant amount of evidence
> suggesting the FBI knows more about the case than it is admitting?
>
> New York City has a new mayor and a new police commissioner, Eric
> Adams and Keechant Sewell. Both have promised an era of transparency
> and racial healing in New York, and recent polling shows strong
> support for their pro-cop, tough-on-crime agenda. But the Cardillo
> affair is unfinished business, a restless ghost that comes back to
> haunt New York at its worst moments. Adams and Sewell should haul in
> the NYPD officials responsible for those “ongoing investigation”
> statements and get some answers. The coverup should end. The true
> story of the Harlem Mosque Incident should be made public. Remember
> Cardillo. Fifty years is enough.
>
> Until next week ...

[INSIDE JW] BIDEN’S 'MINISTRY OF TRUTH' & ELON MUSK, BIDEN ADMIN TARGETS O’KEEFE/PROJECT VERITAS, BIOLAB CONCERNS [Weekly Update] [=] JUDICIAL WATCH SUES DOJ, AND HHS FOR COMMUNICATIONS ABOUT PROJECT VERITAS From midnight raids to legal maneuvering, the government has been attacking Project Veritas for years. We need to know the details of any Biden administration discussions targeting the journalists at Project Veritas. We filed three FOIA lawsuits against Departments of Justice (DOJ) and Health and Human Services (HHS) for communications about Project Veritas with Pfizer, the New York Times and other outside groups (Judicial Watch v Department of Justice [] (No. 1:22-cv-01035)) (Judicial Watch v Department of Health and Human Services [] (No. 1:22-cv-01033)) (Judicial Watch v Department of Justice [] (No. 1:22-cv-01034)). The lawsuit (No. 1:22-cv-01035) about the FBI’s communications with Pfizer about Project Veritas was filed after the DOJ failed to respond to a December 21, 2021, FOIA request for: All records of communications between officials in the FBI, including officials in the offices of the FBI New York Field Office on the one hand, and employees and representatives of Pfizer Inc. on the other hand, regarding Project Veritas founder James O’Keefe and/or Project Veritas. The lawsuit (No. 1:22-cv-01033) regarding Phoenix Indian Medical Center communications about Project Veritas was filed after HHS failed to respond to an October 18, 2021, FOIA request for: All records of communications between PIMC officials and/or employees regarding, concerning, Jodi O’Malley, James O’Keefe and/or Project Veritas. The lawsuit (No. 1:22-cv-01034) about the FBI’s communications with the New York Times about Project Veritas was filed after the DOJ failed to respond to a November 10, 2021, FOIA request for: All records of communications between officials in the FBI, including officials in the offices of the FBI Director, FBI Deputy Director, Office of General Counsel, Office of Public Affairs, and/or the FBI New York Field Office on the one hand, and employees, contractors, and representatives of The New York Times on the other hand, regarding the FBI search warrants and raid on the residence of Project Veritas journalist Spencer Meads on November 4, 2021. All records of communications between officials in the FBI, including officials in the offices of the FBI Director, FBI Deputy Director, Office of General Counsel, Office of Public Affairs, and/or the FBI New York Field Office on the one hand, and employees, contractors, and representatives of The New York Times on the other hand, regarding the FBI search warrants and raid on the residence of Project Veritas founder James O’Keefe on November 6, 2021. In January 2022, we announced [] that the FBI told us in a response to a FOIA request that it has communications from Pfizer in an investigative file targeting Project Veritas. In October 2021, Project Veritas [==], a nonprofit investigative journalism organization, published two viral stories [here [=] and here [=]] about the Pfizer COVID vaccine. SAFETY LAPSES AT BIOSAFETY LABS HANDLING DANGEROUS AGENTS AND TOXINS The federal government monitors activity at 244 [==] secure, high-containment biosafety laboratories on U.S. soil that handle dangerous viruses and bacteria [==]. We’ve discovered several mishaps, human errors, animal escapes, improper and defective personal protective equipment incidents, facility equipment failures and containment failures at these labs. We learned this in 25 pages [==] of redacted records and communications from the Federal Select Agent Program (FSAP). The records were produced through our January 25, 2022, Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to the Federal Select Agent Program for: Any and all records maintained by the U.S. Department of Agriculture including memoranda, draft memoranda, reports, email communications, email chains, investigative reports and other communications or data concerning accidents, investigations, incidents, spills, loss, theft, near miss hazardous events, and enforcement actions regarding any Select Agent or Toxin at Biosafety Level (BSL) 2, BSL 3 or BSL 4 laboratories. The Federal Select Agent Program [=] “is jointly comprised of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Division of Select Agents and Toxins and the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service/Division of Agricultural Select Agents and Toxins. The Federal Select Agent Program oversees the possession, use and transfer of biological select agents and toxins, which have the potential to pose a severe threat to public, animal or plant health or to animal or plant products.” Here are some of the details of what we learned. On March 11, 2021, the Federal Select Agent Program sent a letter [] to a recipient whose name is redacted titled “Suspension of Registration.” The letter advises the entity that their certificate of registration “to possess, use, and transfer select agents and toxins is suspended” due to “failure to comply with the regulatory requirements.” The letter further states: [T]he APHIS/CDC [Animal and Plant Health Inspection [=]] ... reports and notification of inventory discrepancies made in January 2019, October – November 2020, and most recently in January 2021, indicate systemic noncompliance with inventory record keeping and effective training requirements that would prevent these repeated occurrences. Despite written assurances by the Responsible Official (RO) after each aforementioned incident that staff had been retrained on inventory practices and reminded of [the importance] of proper communication [redacted] continued to report inventory discrepancies. Specifically, [redacted] systemic noncompliance with the ed by the following: The specifics of each of the incidents are redacted. The letter orders the entity to cease all activities with select agents and toxins except a “vial-by-vial inventory.” Corrective actions were required to be completed by August 11, 2021, or the certificate of registration could be revoked, resulting in “all select agents and toxins a [redacted] will need to be transferred to a registered facility or destroyed.” On March 11, 2020, the Agriculture Select Agent Services (AgSAS [=]) sends a letter [] to a recipient whose name is redacted titled “Corrective Action Plan (CAP).” The letter indicates the “USDA-APHIS [Animal and Plant Health Inspection] Investigative Enforcement Services (IES)” sends a letter on February 27, 2020, “in which [redacted] agreed to meet with the CAP requirements outlined in [an] IES letter.” The March letter provides notice that failure to follow the plan of action could result in the “suspension or revocation of [redacted] certificate of registration for the possession, use and transfer of select agents and toxins....” On February 19, 2021, Animal and Plant Health Inspection Services, sends a letter [] to a recipient whose name is redacted that includes the subject line “Suspension of Registration.” The letter advises the entity that their certificate of registration to possess, use, and transfer select agents and toxins is suspended due to failure to comply with regulatory requirements related to registration and restricted experiments; responsible official, and theft, loss or release; security; biosafety-general; incident response; training; and records keeping observed during a January 19-22, 2021, compliance inspection. On July 19, 2019, then-CDC Director Dr. Robert R. Redfield sends a letter [==] to then-Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Alex M. Azar II titled: “Report to Congress on the Notifications of Theft, Loss, or Release of Select Agents and Toxins for Calendar Year 2018 – Decision:” Between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2018, the Select Agent Regulatory Programs at USDA and HHS received eight reports of BSAT [biological select agents and toxins] loss, 193 reports of BSAT release. and zero reports of a theft of a BSAT for calendar year (CY) 2018. There were eight reports of a Joss (failure to account for BSAT), all from registered entities. [the Federal Select Agent Program] refers all reports of a BSAT loss to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). In CY 2018, the FBI determined that there was no criminal nexus for any of the eight reported losses. None of the reported losses resulted in a risk to public or agricultural health; and There were 193 reports of a release (occupational exposure or release of BSJ\ T outside of the primary barriers of the biocontainment area). Of these reports, 66 reports were submitted by registered entities and 127 reports were from non-registered entities. None of the reported releases resulted in illnesses, deaths, or transmissions among workers or outside of a laboratory into the surrounding environment or community. A chart within the report reveals the release of biological select agents and toxins were attributed to: one bite or scratch from an infected animal; 138 manipulations of select agents or toxins outside a biological safety cabinet or other equipment designed to protect from exposure; nine equipment or mechanical failures; 22 failures of personal protective equipment; 10 needle sticks or other exposures; nine spills of select agents; and four escaped animals. A report [=] dated July 6, 2020, is titled “Report to Congress: Notifications of Theft, Loss, or Release of Select Agents and Toxins for Calendar Year 2019.” A summary of the report reads: During CY [calendar year 2019], [the Federal Select Agent Program] received 13 reports of losses, 219 reports of releases, and zero reports of thefts. None of the releases resulted in illnesses, deaths, or transmissions to/or among workers. nor was there a BSAT [biological select agents and toxins] transmission to the outside of a laboratory into the surrounding environment or community. The FBI investigated all 13 report of losses and, in all cases, determined there was no criminal nexus. A chart within the report indicates the releases of select agents or toxins were attributed to the following: four bites or scratches from an infected animal; 140 manipulations of select agents or toxins outside a biological safety cabinet or other equipment designed to protect from exposure; one decontamination failure; 10 instances of deviation from standard laboratory operating procedures, such as not wearing the appropriate personal protective equipment or other safety violation; 16 equipment or mechanical failures; 21 failures of personal protective equipment; two failures in performing inactivation methods or removal methods for select agents; 13 needle sticks or other exposures; 10 spills of select agent; and two escaped animals. A report [=] from the USDA and HHS dated June 2021 is titled “Report to Congress: Notifications of Theft, Loss, or Release of Select Agents and Toxins for Calendar Year 2020.” A summary of the report indicates: During [calendar year 2020], [the Federal Select Agent Program] received 13 reports of losses, 158 reports of releases, and no reports of theft of [biological select agents and toxins]. None of the reported releases resulted in death or transmission among workers nor transmission to the outside of a laboratory into the surrounding environment or community. FSAP [the Federal Select Agent Program] received one report from a non-registered entity of a release that resulted in an occupational illness in one worker that made a full recovery after receiving medical treatment. The FBI investigated all 13 reports of losses and, in all cases, determined there was no criminal nexus. A chart within the report notes that the releases of select agent or toxin were attributed to the following: one bite or scratch from an infected animal; 92 manipulations of select agents or toxins outside a biological safety cabinet or other equipment designed to protect from exposure; one decontamination failure; five instances of deviation from standard laboratory operating procedures such, as not wearing the appropriate personal protective equipment or other safety violation; 19 equipment or mechanical failures; 13 failures of personal protective equipment; two failures in performing a validated inactivation or [biological select agents and toxins] removal method; 13 needle sticks or other exposures; 17 spills of select agent; and one escaped animal. The report explains that one of the exposures resulted in an illness of one worker after exposure to Coxiella Burnetii [==. “The source of the infection was attributed to contact with infected animals in the performance of the worker’s duties. The worker received medical treatment and fully recovered from the illness. The entity notified all workers potentially exposed to the infected worker and found no evidence of disease transmission to others.” These documents uncover a pattern of serious safety issues in biolabs here on U.S. soil. And, given these issues here at home, one can imagine the safety issues of labs the U.S. funds abroad. For example, in June 2021, through a FOIA lawsuit, we uncovered [=] a January 19, 2018, State Department cable [=] from the US Embassy in Beijing about the Wuhan Institute of Virology with the subject “China Opens First Bio Safety Level 4 Laboratory” that includes a section titled “Unclear Guidelines on Virus Access and a Lack of Trained Talent Impede Research,” which notes in its introduction that “its current productivity is limited by a shortage of highly trained technicians and investigators required to safely operate a BSL-4 laboratory and a lack of clarity in related Chinese government policies and guidelines.” BIDEN DOJ SAYS SHORTER SENTENCES WILL PROMOTE ‘EQUITY’ While violent crime is rising, according [=] to a top FBI official, the Biden Justice Department is busying itself by telling prosecutors to ignore maximum sentences in the interest of “fairness.” Our Corruption Chronicles blog looks into [==] this dangerous madness. The government agency charged with enforcing the law, ensuring public safety against foreign threats, and controlling crime has been quite busy formulating an official strategy to “advance equity for marginalized and underserved communities.” Made public this month, the policy is known as the Department of Justice Equity Action Plan [] and among its key initiatives is a reform in law enforcement practices that directs federal prosecutors to ignore maximum sentencing under the law. That will help “avoid unwarranted disparities, promote fair outcomes in sentencing, and seek justice in every case,” according to the new Biden administration plan. The DOJ brags that it issued prosecutors guidance requiring decisions about charging, plea agreements, and advocacy at sentencing to be based on “an individualized assessment of relevant facts, and not to reflexively rely on the maximum punishments allowable under law.” The DOJ assures that it will continue to pursue policies that promote equitable law enforcement practices. The agency’s new Justice Equity Action Plan also creates a new Language Access Coordinator to report hate crimes in at least 10 languages, including six of the most frequently spoken Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI). An Anti-Hate Coordinator will oversee a new division and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), which operates under the DOJ, has been directed to designate hate crimes as “one of its highest-level national threat priorities.” The change will force the FBI to make hate crimes a focus for all of its 56 field offices, according to the new policy. The DOJ will also award over $21 million to help state and local agencies as well as community organizations “address an alarming rise in violent and property crimes committed on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, or disability.” A new Office for Access to Justice will help disenfranchised minorities navigate the justice system by offering language and cultural access, which the DOJ claims will ensure economic opportunity and fairness and pursue racial equity. Under the new plan the DOJ will ensure that approximately $4 billion in grants awarded annually for justice-related programs is administered in a way that is inclusive of historically underserved and marginalized populations and implemented in a nondiscriminatory manner. Every year the agency doles the money out to community policing services, correctional and juvenile justice facilities, drug and mental health courts, services for crime victims and law enforcement wellness services. The grant programs “present a significant opportunity to further equity across a broad spectrum of services,” the new DOJ plan states, adding that grant recipients will be directed to take actions to promote greater equity in their communities and strengthen the agency’s enforcement of nondiscrimination mandates. The DOJ will also give more money to “entities serving communities that historically have had fewer opportunities to access and benefit from federal financial assistance.” This includes prioritizing funding for “culturally specific” organizations that provide “culturally relevant and linguistically specific services and resources to cultural groups” such as Latinos and blacks. The new DOJ plan is part of the Biden administration’s sweeping effort to advance racial equity and support for underserved communities through the federal government. The costly initiative was launched back in January 2021 when the president issued an executive order [==] claiming that “entrenched disparities” in laws, public policies, and private institutions have denied equal opportunity to individuals and communities and that the health and climate crises have exposed inequities while a “historic movement for justice has highlighted the unbearable human costs of systemic racism.” Therefore, the executive order states, the federal government should pursue a “comprehensive approach to advancing equity for all, including people of color and others who have been historically underserved, marginalized, and adversely affected by persistent poverty and inequality.” It further says that “by advancing equity across the Federal Government, we can create opportunities for the improvement of communities that have been historically underserved, which benefits everyone.” Many key federal agencies have already implemented racial equity plans as per Biden’s order. The Department of Labor has dedicated $260 million [=] to promote “equitable access” to government unemployment benefits by addressing disparities in the administration and delivery of money by race ethnicity and language proficiency. The Treasury Department named its first ever racial equity chief, a veteran La Raza official who spent a decade at the nation’s most influential open borders group. The Department of Defense (DOD) is using outrageous anti-bias materials that indoctrinate troops with anti-American and racially inflammatory training on diversity topics. The U. S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) created an equity commission to address longstanding inequities in agriculture. The nation’s medical research agency has a special minority health and health disparities division that recently issued a study [] declaring COVID-19 exacerbated preexisting resentment against racial/ethnic minorities and marginalized communities. JUDICIAL WATCH DEMANDS ANSWERS IN COLD CASE MURDER OF NYPD OFFICER Should we give up on justice even a half century after a murder was committed? No, we shouldn’t – and especially when it appears there is an official coverup still underway. Micah Morrison, our chief investigative reporter, reports the details [= our Investigative Bulletin. Fifty years ago this month, NYPD Patrolman Phillip Cardillo was gunned down inside Louis Farrakhan’s Nation of Islam Mosque in Harlem. No one ever did a day in jail for the crime. Is justice in the Cardillo case still possible? The episode quickly became known as “the Harlem Mosque Incident” and was immediately engulfed in controversy, with rank-and-file cops ordered off the crime scene, a riot in Harlem, racial tensions, and a NYPD coverup. An alleged shooter was brought to trial in 1976, but a Judicial Watch investigation decades later revealed that key evidence was buried, never making it to investigators and prosecutors. The defendant was acquitted at a second trial, after the first trial resulted in a hung jury. At that point, a special prosecutor stepped in. He concluded in a 1980 report that there was “a concerted and orchestrated effort by members and former members of the Police Department to impede the investigation into the murder of Patrolman Philip Cardillo.” That is, there was a coverup. By the NYPD. Of the murder of one of its own. The case seemed to die. But one cop would not let it go. NYPD Detective Randy Jurgensen was the key investigator in the Cardillo affair. A legendary figure in New York law-enforcement, Jurgensen pursued the case through the two trials to a bitter end. In 2006, he published “Circle of Six,” a hard-hitting expose that accused New York’s political and police establishment of a “purposeful negligence of duty.” Soon after, then-NYPD Police Commissioner Ray Kelly ordered the NYPD’s Major Case Squad to take another look at the case. Judicial Watch got involved in the new Cardillo investigation. We uncovered critical documents in the case—some never before seen, some lost for decades—including a White House tape of President Richard Nixon and FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover launching a secret program to hunt down cop killers; a secret NYPD report on the killing, known as “the Blue Book,” that was withheld from the department’s own investigators and Manhattan trial prosecutors; the long-lost special prosecutor’s report that raised questions about NYPD obstruction of justice; and FBI documents revealing a network of (unnamed) informants in the case and hinting at possible dirty tricks that may have drawn police to the Harlem mosque that fateful day in April. Read Judicial Watch’s investigative report here. Seeking to learn more about the FBI’s role at the Harlem mosque, Judicial Watch filed a Freedom of Information Act request for “all records concerning the Nation of Islam Mosque #7 in Harlem... [including but not limited to] all informant, wiretap, electronic surveillance, and physical surveillance records.” The FBI denied it had any records related to the mosque. Judicial Watch was not satisfied with the FBI response and we filed a FOIA lawsuit seeking a more thorough search of records. But no new records were obtained from the FBI in the case. The NYPD took an even more brazen approach when we sought case documents under New York’s Freedom of Information Law. The NYPD turned us down, claiming it did not have to provide the records because the Cardillo case was still “active and ongoing.” Freedom of information laws have a standard exemption from disclosure of material that could impact an ongoing investigation. But at the time we filed the FOIL request, the Cardillo case was forty-eight years old. There was zero evidence that the case was active and ongoing. The NYPD’s refusal to provide any information appeared to be an extension of a decades-old coverup. The coverup was first experienced by early investigators on the case, including Jurgensen, and first officially noted in the 1980 special prosecutor’s report. Judicial Watch decided not to take “no” for an answer. We sued the NYPD for documents related to the Cardillo investigation. The case went all the way up to New York’s high court. But in the end, we lost. The commanding officer of the NYPD Major Case Squad supervising the case claimed under oath that the Cardillo murder “is an open investigation and remains actively pursued by the NYPD.” The court noted that the NYPD also “submitted...information obtained from the detective leading an active, ongoing investigation into the homicide, which included receiving tips from informants and conducting interviews of potential witnesses.” The court ruled that the NYPD “properly withheld the requested materials” based on NYPD statements that disclosure would interfere with an ongoing investigation. Read the full court decision here [=]. If the NYPD is to be believed, an active pursuit of Cardillo’s killer was underway. But it’s been more than two years since the New York court, accepting NYPD assurances, rejected Judicial Watch’s FOIL request. Is that “active investigation” into the Cardillo killing still “ongoing?” What has been accomplished? Fifty years on, is justice for Phil Cardillo still possible? “Remember Cardillo” remains a rallying cry for generations of New York City cops—a searing reminder of the dangers of the job, of racial strife, and what happens when the brass throws a beat cop under the bus. Critical questions in the case remain unresolved. Who killed Cardillo? Who called in the fake “officer in distress” phone call that lured Cardillo to the Harlem mosque? Who ordered the ubiquitous Nation of Islam guards off the front doors of the mosque that morning, allowing Cardillo and other officers to rush in to what appears to have been an ambush? What was the role, if any, of the FBI in the case? What about the significant amount of evidence suggesting the FBI knows more about the case than it is admitting? New York City has a new mayor and a new police commissioner, Eric Adams and Keechant Sewell. Both have promised an era of transparency and racial healing in New York, and recent polling shows strong support for their pro-cop, tough-on-crime agenda. But the Cardillo affair is unfinished business, a restless ghost that comes back to haunt New York at its worst moments. Adams and Sewell should haul in the NYPD officials responsible for those “ongoing investigation” statements and get some answers. The coverup should end. The true story of the Harlem Mosque Incident should be made public. Remember Cardillo. Fifty years is enough. Until next week ... body:
| Hi there,

I’m Dr. Ashley Hink. I am a trauma surgeon, violence researcher, and I work with Dr. Annie Andrews.

Working with Annie, I’ve seen her dedication to Lowcountry children and families.

This job isn’t pretty. Far too often, we see children and teenagers, with their whole lives ahead of them, come to our hospitals with preventable injuries from violence and firearms. These are children who should be learning how to ride their bikes, teenagers who should be learning to drive and planning for their futures. But because too many of our lawmakers prioritize the gun lobby over common sense gun legislation and investment in violence prevention strategies, their futures are taken from them.

It will always be heartbreaking to care for children and teenagers with bullet holes. This work is hard, but I am so grateful to have Annie by my side in this fight. Day in and day out, she shows resilience and patience, and gives her patients and her community hope. For years, she has committed herself to creating a safer community for all of us, and promoting safe, responsible firearm ownership.

Her opponents don’t hold these values. They are gun extremists, beholden to the gun lobby, who do not engage in serious, evidence-based solutions — many of which are supported by the majority of South Carolinians in both parties.

Firearms are now the leading cause of death for children and teens in the U.S. _If our elected representatives value the gun lobby over children’s lives, and don’t think this is a priority worth addressing with**real solutions,** they shouldn’t be representing us._

**[I know Annie is the representative we need for the Lowcountry. She’ll bring the skills and passion she has from years of working to heal and advocate for the safety of our kids to the job. But first, she has to win. clean_body: Hello, In a moment, I’m going to ask you to make a donation to my campaign against Chuck Grassley and help me protect our Democratic Senate majority. But before I do, let me explain why your donation to turn Iowa’s Senate seat blue is so important right now. I am a hard target for a GOP attack ad. I was born and raised in rural northwest Iowa, and I served our country for nearly 4 decades in the U.S. Navy. From enlisting on scholarship in college to retiring as a three-star Admiral, none of that matters because the GOP’s Super PACs will drum up a misleading ad and even attack my service. In my last election, Super PACs spent millions of dollars against me. And this time, Mitch McConnell and his billionaire buddies are raising even more to spin lying tales about me on TVs all across Iowa. There’s one reason: Mitch McConnell is alarmed because I’m the guy who can defeat Chuck Grassley and turn Iowa blue. I’m it. And if I do win, Democrats will hold onto our Democratic majority in the Senate. Iowa was one of the closest Senate races in 2020, and the latest poll from the Des Moines Register shows a paltry 27% of Iowa voters want to reelect Grassley. I’m happy for the fight ahead, but I’m not taking money from corporate PACs. Instead, I’m counting on grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win and turn Iowa blue. We’re less than 24 hours away from our important end-of-month fundraising deadline of the entire campaign, and right now we’re still very short of our $500,000 goal. | Peter \-
We're coming down to the wire and the future of Pennsylvania and America is coming down to how we close this month. If we don't hit our goal it could be the end. It's that simple.
The odds are in our favor. We're surging in the polls while everyone else remains stagnant, but we need to make a STRONG, focused push right now with all hands on deck. But polls don't win at the ballot box and now is not the time to rest easy. Patrick Murray, director of the independent Monmouth University Polling Institute summed it up best:
"This is the kind of environment where a number of candidates could emerge as the nominee. Oz has the highest name recognition but also the highest negatives. If McCormick and Oz beat each other up, though, Barnette could realistically end up on top."
While this campaign is in a statistical tie for first, the two most recognizable names are spending MILLIONS of their funds on ATTACK ADS against EACH OTHER. This campaign isn't spending all of YOUR money that way, this campaign is focused on outreach -- meeting and listening to the people of the great Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
If Mehmet Oz and Beijing Dave McCormick continue fighting each other in the corner of the room, we can walk right past them. They're so concerned with each other that they're ignoring the voice of the voters. These carpetbaggers spending all their money and time on attacking each other show that their priorities AREN'T the people of Pennsylvania, but rather winning for the sake of victory.
Their victories have defeated them. Their peace has made them soft.
The people of Pennsylvania don't need a soft conservative who has no intention of CONSERVING any piece of the American way of life -- they want a FIGHTER who will defend their rights and freedoms. I know you want real representation, and through this campaign YOU CAN HAVE IT.
---

clean_body: I’m ready to serve as your First District problem-solver | | | | | ---|---|--- Peter, Energy and food insecurity are not just some hypothetical issues that should be used to score points against your political opponents. Food insecurity is a real threat worldwide with the potential to ravage countries and tear apart their social fabric. With this level of angst in the world, it’s shocking that President Biden, instead of calling for national unity, pointed the finger at others for high gas prices and wants to use up our existing strategic petroleum reserves. The United States must quickly tap into multiple energy sources to ramp back up our output levels and get us back to a position of economic strength. What Biden refuses to acknowledge is that a weak America results in an unstable world. I am not a politician, but a lifelong advocate with deep roots in our communities and experience in the private sector. Our Congressional District right now is without representation in Washington D.C. We need a strong conservative voice with experience in standing up and being heard. With your help, I am ready to serve as your First District problem-solver. body:
In a moment, I'm going to ask you to make a donation to my re-election campaign before our end-of-month fundraising deadline at midnight. But first, I wanted to share why this 2023 governor's race is so important. Hey Peter,

In a moment, I'm going to ask you to make a donation to my re-election campaign before our end-of-month fundraising deadline at midnight. But first, I wanted to share why this 2023 governor's race is so important.

Over the last two years, we've made a lot of progress for Kentuckians. We've restored voting rights to hundreds of thousands of Kentuckians, fought this pandemic, had the best economic development year on record, and so much more.

The future of our Commonwealth is too bright for us to not fight as hard as we can for it. That's why it's crucial we win this governor's race next year to protect and expand upon the progress we've made, but it won't be easy.

In 2019, we won this race by just over 5,000 votes. I already have two Republican challengers, and a wealthy, self-funded opponent may soon enter the race. It's clear we have a tough re-election campaign ahead of us.

That's why I'm counting on the support of this grassroots team to help us reach our end-of-month fundraising deadline by midnight to ensure we have the resources necessary to continue delivering progress to folks across the Commonwealth.

**Will you make a donation to my re-election campaign before our end-of-month deadline to help me protect the progress we're making for Kentuckians? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beshear-q2-2022?refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/44748262/342948677/-1274636763?refcode=em22_220430_eom2_fnd_gq_act___ab_ettx&utm_campaign=em22_220430_eom2_fnd_gq_act___ab_ettx&utm_medium=email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85MzM0NiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5OGFmMjhlOC04ZGM4LWVjMTEtOTk3ZS0yODE4NzhiODNkOGEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=YPxYgSC3UwWsDcryCymvu44Qr0GooRPqd4eidVz6vuY=)**

clean_body: When Donald Trump was President and Republicans controlled the Senate, it was like pulling teeth to try to get things done. | | | Derek, It’s hard to believe it, but we’re already well into our second year of a Democratic majority in Congress and a Democratic President in the White House. And it’s incredible how much things have changed in that short amount of time. When Donald Trump was President and Republicans controlled the Senate, it was like pulling teeth to try to get things done. True, we had a few moments of bipartisanship, like when the Senate passed my historic National Parks bill. But more often than not we were fighting to prevent things like repealing the Affordable Care Act. It was a hard time for so many Virginians who sent me to the Senate to make meaningful change. Since Democrats took the majority, we’ve made real progress to combat the pandemic and get our economy back on track. But the truth is, our Senate majority is at risk. The experts are saying it, the polls are showing it, and it’s on us to make sure we hang on this November. = We got through a huge, once in a generation investment in our infrastructure. We’ve made critical investments in our cyber security. We’ve expanded access to broadband internet. We’ve helped put more Virginians and more Americans back to work. I’m so proud of what we’ve accomplished because I know it’s what you sent me to the Senate to do. But I’m not nearly done. Right now I’m working on a China competition bill that will bring more manufacturing jobs to Virginia and ease our supply chain issues. I’m pushing to cap insulin copay costs — my daughter is a type-1 diabetic, so this one is really personal to me.
